claims.statement: Galpi touches exactly two outside services at runtime — Hugging Face (first-prepare model downloads only) and an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API (AI minutes refinement only) — while recording and transcription are fully local; the webview CSP permits no network beyond the Tauri IPC bridge.

scripts/stage-sidecars.ts pins uv 0.12.5 for aarch64-apple-darwin and verifies the SHA-256 of both the GitHub release archive and the extracted binary against hardcoded checksums before staging src-tauri/binaries/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin; staging is idempotent (a matching existing binary skips the download, a mismatch is deleted and re-fetched), and the script runs before every dev/build via tauri.conf.json beforeDevCommand/beforeBuildCommand.

stage-sidecars.ts also refreshes src-tauri/resources/worker with the galpi_worker source (excluding bytecode caches) plus the four requirements/lock files, whose locks are what the installer reads; at runtime uv_binary() resolves the bundled uv from src-tauri/binaries in debug builds and from beside the executable in release builds (tauri.conf.json externalBin).

Each engine preset gets an app-private Python 3.12 virtualenv provisioned by uv: `uv python install 3.12` into UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR, `uv venv --clear` (so a failed first attempt leaves nothing that blocks retries), then `uv pip install -r <lock>` — WhisperX from requirements.lock with --require-hashes, Qwen3 from requirements-qwen3.lock; the readiness marker is written only after pip succeeds.

The worker environment is constructed rather than inherited (env_clear + envs): UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed admits only uv-managed interpreters, the engine bin dir is prepended to PATH so the linked ffmpeg resolves, and HF_HOME/TORCH_HOME/UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR all stay inside the app data root so deleting Galpi's folder reclaims the gigabytes.

WhisperX and Qwen3 live in separate virtualenvs (engine/.venv vs engine/qwen3/.venv) so the presets never share dependency versions, and src-tauri/build.rs fingerprints worker/requirements.txt and requirements-qwen3.txt with FNV-1a at compile time; the hash is baked into each preset's readiness marker, so editing a pin invalidates the installed venv by itself and the next prepare reinstalls it.
Minutes refinement always runs under the WhisperX preset's interpreter (paths.python) because the assistant client is stdlib urllib only — no provider SDK exists in either dependency set.

ffmpeg is not a separate download: both requirement sets pin imageio-ffmpeg, prepare links its binary into the preset's engine bin dir (symlink with copy+chmod 0755 fallback), that link is exactly what the ffmpeg_ready readiness check inspects, and PATH prepending makes every worker ffmpeg invocation (decode and silencedetect) resolve to it.

Model needs are two presets sharing one gated diarizer — Qwen3 uses Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B, Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B and pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1; WhisperX uses mobiuslabsgmbh/faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo, kresnik/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-korean and the same pyannote model — and models_ready is file-based: a valid manifest (protocol 1 plus engine version) plus the presence of models--Org--Name hub directories derived mechanically from the repo ids, with the converted MLX weights file additionally required for Qwen3.

The pyannote gate is satisfied by a fine-grained, read-only token (hf_ prefix) scoped to that one repository and needed only for the first download; the settings sheet's token guide documents this and says the token may be left empty once access was approved or the model is already on the Mac, and the model-access button opens the Hugging Face model page through the opener plugin — the webview's only outbound navigation.

prepare_qwen3_models downloads the ASR and aligner snapshots concurrently with two snapshot_download workers and routes tqdm through DownloadReporter, which sums per-file bars into one GB figure and throttles phase events to one per second over the 10–40% band — without it the setup bar would sit frozen for the whole multi-gigabyte fetch.

The downloaded Qwen3 ASR snapshot is quantized once into 8-bit MLX weights (group size 64) at cache/mlx/qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit via a .partial staging directory moved into place with os.replace, carrying tokenizer/config sidecars and quantization_config.json so Session(model=<dir>) loads fully offline; verify_qwen3_session then transcribes one second of silence to move conversion failures into prepare, and the gated diarizer is warmed once with the token so real meetings pay no download cost.

prepare_whisperx_models warms models implicitly through the libraries — whisperx.load_model('large-v3-turbo', 'cpu', int8), the Korean alignment model, and DiarizationPipeline('pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1') — with alignment and diarization getting exactly one MPS→CPU retry each, every model dropped with gc.collect() between stages, before writing models/ready.json and emitting the prepared event.

Before WhisperX model prepare, import_standard_cache copies the three known hub directories from ~/.cache/huggingface/hub into the app cache using hard links (copy fallback), recreating symlinks only when their canonical target stays inside the source repository (an escaping link is an error); the import is best-effort — a failure is logged as an event and treated as zero imported so prepare continues on the normal download path.

can_use_offline_cache is true only when all three model directories imported and the configured token is blank; only then does model prepare gain HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 — a complete tokenless cache needs no network, and a token would suggest the user intends gated access.

The Hugging Face token is scoped to prepare only: Application::prepare fills a missing token from settings, setup passes it only into the model environment (process_environment inserts HF_TOKEN for a non-blank trimmed value), while the install environment and every transcription environment are built with None — and Qwen3 transcription instead forces both offline flags because it runs only after the readiness gate, so no network round trip can occur mid-meeting.

Hugging Face failures surface rather than stall: worker exceptions become one ENGINE_ERROR protocol error event via main()'s catch-all, worker stderr is batched into log events so thousands of uv/pip/tqdm lines do not flood the webview, and the prepare verdict is recomputed from markers and manifests — anything short of ready fails SETUP_INCOMPLETE regardless of exit code, and because every stage re-runs status() first, re-running prepare retries only what is missing.

The minutes request is POST {base_url}/chat/completions with stream=true, Accept: text/event-stream, Authorization: Bearer <key>, temperature 0.2 and a 600-second timeout; the base URL defaults to https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4 (overridable via GALPI_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL), the model defaults to glm-5.3-flash on both frontend and worker sides, GLM models on the default endpoint get max_tokens 131072 while everything else gets 32768, and reasoning_effort is sent only when one of low/medium/high/max was chosen so other providers receive a clean OpenAI-compatible body.

The allowed reasoning efforts (low, medium, high, max) are enforced on both sides: AssistantSettings::trimmed lowercases the saved value and drops anything else, and the worker silently ignores an unknown GALPI_ASSISTANT_REASONING_EFFORT rather than sending it.

consume_assistant_stream keeps progress monotonic: reasoning_content deltas hold the percent at the band start while reporting the live reasoning length, content deltas map accumulated characters onto the 35–88% band throttled to one event per 4096 characters or 1.5 seconds, and long-meeting map/reduce (16,000-character chunks, three concurrent map workers) reports per completed chunk instead of characters because concurrent streams would make a character count jump backwards.

Every minutes-API failure reaches the UI with the provider's own message preserved: an error payload inside the SSE stream raises immediately with the JSON-serialized error, HTTPError includes the status code and the first 500 characters of the response body, URLError includes the underlying reason, and an empty document names its finish_reason ('length' and 'content_filter' get dedicated operator-facing messages); all become RuntimeError → one ENGINE_ERROR protocol event → a job error event rendered in the augment panel.

The assistant key is read at the only moment it is needed: load_assistant deliberately returns api_key: None with just the api_key_stored boolean, refine_transcript calls load_assistant_api_key and fails ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING when it was never saved, the key travels to the worker via GALPI_ASSISTANT_API_KEY in assistant_environment (never an argument vector), and the worker still refuses with INVALID_INPUT if the variable is missing.

Sensitive refinement context that is not a credential — background text, the selected participant roster, the glossary — is handed to the worker through 0600 temporary files created with create_new (refusing to write through an existing file) and deleted after the run, never through the argument vector where a process listing would expose it.

Both credentials (Hugging Face token, assistant API key) flow through the SecretStore trait; production wires SettingsFile — plaintext fields in settings.json written atomically with a .json.part temporary chmod'ed 0600 before rename — because macOS ties Keychain item access to the code signature that stored the item and Galpi ships ad-hoc signed; the compiled Keychain store (service com.m16khb.galpi, accounts hugging-face-token / assistant-api-key, read failures treated as nothing stored) is kept for a one-line swap in LocalSettingsStore::new once a stable Developer ID signature exists.

Whichever store backs it, secret handling has three invariants: reads are cached per launch (each real keychain access can prompt the user, and the sheet autosaves on every keystroke), a value identical to the cached one is never rewritten (a no-op write would re-prompt for authorization), and legacy plaintext found in the settings file is migrated into the store on first read and scrubbed from the file when the store holds the secret itself.

The CSP in tauri.conf.json restricts the webview to connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost (with object-src/frame-src/form-action locked down), so no integration is reachable from the UI; all network happens inside spawned worker processes whose environment the host fully constructs — the standing extension rule is that new integrations live in outbound adapters behind a port, with credentials passed via environment or SecretStore, never from the webview or domain/application code.
